key_insight: This paper maps out key design choices in continuous diffusion language models (CDLMs), showing that training performance depends strongly on specific levers such as self-conditioning. It helps clarify how to make continuous diffusion more competitive, controllable, and efficient for language generation.
problem_solved: CDLMs are promising, but researchers still lack a clear understanding of which training and architectural choices actually matter most. The paper addresses this gap by studying the design space and identifying the most influential factors for improving CDLM performance.
method: Systematically analyze the CDLM design space with a focus on self-conditioning and related training levers.
Compare how different settings affect model quality, sampling behavior, and controllability.
Use empirical evaluation to identify which choices improve continuous diffusion language modeling most effectively.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work provides a clearer roadmap for building stronger CDLMs without relying on trial-and-error. It can help accelerate progress toward faster and more controllable language generation systems.
visual_elements: A design-space map showing the main CDLM levers and their relationships
A before/after comparison chart illustrating performance with and without self-conditioning
A pipeline diagram of continuous diffusion training and sampling for language
An icon-based summary of benefits such as speed, controllability, and quality
paper_title: On the Design Space of Continuous Diffusion Language Models
paper_authors: Oscar Davis, Daan Roos, Alice Bizeul, Amitis Shidani, Victor Turrisi
